heard: Galveston's weather chief Isaac Klein promised that a major hurricane was impossible. The city felt safe, expecting the storm to curve toward Florida. Expert Cuban meteorologists knew the monster was heading straight for Texas. Willis Moore blocked their warnings out of professional jealousy. Moore even banned the word hurricane to avoid a panic. On September 8th, 1900, a 15-foot surge swallowed the city. At least 8,000 people perished in America's deadliest natural disaster. Many died believing the man who promised a hurricane was impossible.
